summary: ansible-core 2.19 always uses Jinja native mode, deprecating the template mode setting and removing the final literal-evaluation pass, so playbooks relying on implicit string-to-object conversion need explicit conversions.
questions: Is jinja2_native still configurable in ansible-core 2.19?
Why do my templates return different types after upgrading?
Does Ansible still evaluate template results as Python literals?
Do I need explicit type conversion in templates now?

answer_card.title: Jinja native mode is now required
answer_card.answer_md:
Previously Ansible supported Jinja's string mode (the default) and native mode, and in both cases evaluated final string results as Python literals.

In ansible-core 2.19:
- **Native mode is used exclusively**; the setting that chose the mode is deprecated and has no effect.
- The final literal-evaluation pass is **gone**, removing a common source of confusion, errors and slowness.
- Native types are preserved more reliably.

If a playbook relied on implicit conversion of strings into objects, add an explicit conversion. Some templates that unintentionally turn non-strings into strings may now show different results.
